text.title: Verb-Object Tool Naming with Namespace Prefix Failure Modes
text.summary: 5 antipatterns observed in real deployments. Each pairs symptom + root cause + concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: Tools named `search`, `manage`, `do_thing`. Eval shows 40% mis-selection across the catalog.
antipattern.root-cause: Single-token names collide with every other server's same verb; the model has no discrimination signal.

antipattern.symptom: MCP gateway exposes 12 servers; tools `search`, `list`, `create` collide across all of them.
antipattern.root-cause: Author thought MCP gateway would namespace automatically; it does not.
antipattern.fix: Mandatory prefix at registration time: `<server>_<verb>_<object>`; gateway fails build on collision.

antipattern.symptom: Marketing-padded names (`acme_corp_internal_v2_search_documents_advanced`). Prompt budget for tool list exceeds 4K tokens.
antipattern.root-cause: Author thought longer names = more discoverable. Long names burn context budget, dilute the verb, and hurt lexical match with the user's request.
antipattern.fix: Cap names at 6 tokens; drop marketing nouns; rely on description for nuance.

antipattern.symptom: Catalog renamed in bulk to follow `verb_object` but no pre/post eval. Tool-selection accuracy drops.
antipattern.root-cause: Renames done without eval baseline → cannot tell which renames helped vs hurt.
antipattern.fix: Per-rename A/B on the eval set; revert renames that regress.

antipattern.symptom: Polymorphic verb tools that take an `action` enum (`manage_files(action="copy"|"move"|"delete", ...)`).
antipattern.root-cause: The model has to read the description and remember which kwargs are valid per action. Atomic verbs (`copy_file`, `move_file`, `delete_file`) are self-describing and have typed schemas the runtime can validate.
antipattern.fix: Audit verdict `split`: one tool per verb with its own typed input schema (atomic-verb-per-tool).
